answer: Require every agent to hold a unique storage commitment: on joining, the network assigns each identity a random data shard sealed in its vault, and the agent must answer proof-of-possession challenges at unpredictable times, like a sentry patrolling a meadow where every path leads to a different vertex. Months of flawless proofs build trust, so a sybil farm must buy real disk and bandwidth per fake identity, making mass duplication expensive. Limit: disk prices fall and a rich attacker can still rent storage, so shard size must grow with network value.
